actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This snake occurs in southern Brazil, northeastern Paraguay, and northern Argentina. In Brazil, it is found in southern Bahia, Espíritu Santo, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Sao Paulo, Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul; it extends westward into extreme eastern Mato Grosso and possibly southern Goias. In Argentina it occurs in the province of Misiones. Bothrops jararaca has managed to reach the islands of Sao Sebastiao, Franceses, dos Porcos and Santa Catarina; some of these islands are up to about 35 km offshore. Close relatives that appear to share a common ancestor with this species occurs in Ilhas Queimada Grande and Alcatrazes. Its vertical range is from near sea level to about 1,000 m (Campbell and Lamar 2004).
documentation.population: It is a generally common species in most of its range. There is no information on population trends.
documentation.habitats: This species inhabits tropical deciduous and moist broad-leaved forest and savanna as well as subtropical upland forest. It is said to prefer open areas (such as croplands) near or close to forest (Campbell and Lamar 2004). It is a viviparous species with a biannual reproductive cycle (Giraudo et al. 2012).
documentation.threats: It is hunted and persecuted by people, but on a range-wide scale no major threats are known.
documentation.measures: There are no known species-specific conservation measures in place for this species. It is found in protected areas throughout its range. It is classified as Vulnerable in Argentina (Giraudo et al. 2012).
documentation.use_trade: This species is not utilized or traded.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern because it is widespread and has no known major threats.
